answer: One concrete Sybil defense is device-bound identity: an agent is paid only when its signature includes a fresh secure-enclave quote, and the ledger admits one identity per unique chip measurement. Cloning the software is free, but each extra identity needs its own physical chip, so an attacker building an orchard of fake workers must buy hardware by the thousand and power every unit. A revoked measurement is blacklisted for good, an umber mark no script can scrub away. The cost floor is the retail price of each chip plus energy, so the saffron promise of cheap mass identities never pays.
